 "explanation": "The unit responds to circular, rimmed shapes, especially round dials and gauges seen face-on. These include stopwatches, speedometers, barometers, watch faces and washing-machine portholes, and the response extends more weakly to other round rimmed objects such as cups, bottle caps, discs, buckets and plaques.",
 "evidence": "The top activations (#1, #3, #5, #11, #12, #13, #20) are mostly circular dials with rims, and washing-machine doors (#2, #4) look similar. The lower-ranked images are other round, rimmed objects like mugs, a coffee cup, bottle caps, a CD/vinyl, a lens, a bowl and a round plaque.",
 "missing_data": "Activations on non-circular dials (rectangular gauges) versus plain circles without a dial face would show whether the unit encodes circularity or dial semantics. Spatial activation maps would also help.",
